identity.real_world_identity_notes: Reiza places the Viper GTS-R in its 2005 GT1 class. FIA form GT2-005 originally homologated the Chrysler Corporation Dodge Viper GTS in Group GT2; the differing labels reflect simulator competition context versus the car's original homologation. The exact historical chassis represented by AMS2 has not been established.

wheel_rim.notes: Round rim supported by documented period-spec cockpit photography; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: AMS2 1.6.9.91 accepted sequential-stick shifts without clutch once moving and required clutch engagement to move from a stop.
The observed automatic cut and blip are medium-confidence perceptual tests; no input or engine-throttle telemetry trace was recorded.

FIA homologation documents the original six-speed manual Borg-Warner T56, while Carsport Holland documents that at least one privateer Viper was converted from the Oreca H-pattern arrangement to a Holinger sequential.
AMS2's sequential behavior is historically plausible for a privateer specification, but it must not be generalized to every Viper GTS-R and does not identify Reiza's exact reference chassis.
'Dodge Viper GTS-R - Low Downforce' inherits these verified base controls as an approved aero-package assumption and was not separately live-tested.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with a sequential shifter; the driver manually used the clutch only to move from a stop.
Clutch was required to move from a stop but not for normal running shifts.
Automatic cut and blip were perceived during the live test and remain medium-confidence until telemetry-measured.
'Dodge Viper GTS-R - Low Downforce' is an exact observed identity inheriting the verified base controls; that aero configuration was not separately live-tested.

confidence.basis: Exact identity and sequential/start behavior were observed directly; automatic cut and blip were perceptual rather than telemetry-measured.

claims.basis: Official DLC listing plus exact CarModel, CarId, and GT1_05 class values observed through SimHub 9.11.22.
FIA and contemporary engineering evidence establish the six-speed original configuration; the first-person Carsport account establishes that a privateer sequential conversion existed.

Direct current-game control test, with cut and blip conservatively limited to medium confidence; historical source establishes privateer sequential plausibility rather than an exact Reiza chassis link.
Visual classification from documented cockpit photographs; the exact late privateer reference chassis remains unknown.

notes: This record deliberately preserves the distinction between original FIA homologation, documented privateer conversions, and the behavior of Reiza's simulated representation.
'Dodge Viper GTS-R - Low Downforce' is an exact approved alias whose controls are inherited from the verified base; it has not been separately live-tested.
